text: Python is a programming language created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991.
Monty Python was a British comedy group known for surreal sketch comedy.
BM25 is a probabilistic ranking function used by search engines and information retrieval systems.
TF IDF weights a term using its frequency in a document and its inverse document frequency across the collection.
Dense retrieval represents queries and documents as embeddings so semantically similar text can match even when exact words differ.
Retrieval augmented generation combines external document retrieval with language model generation to produce grounded answers.
Reciprocal rank fusion combines several ranked result lists using reciprocal rank scores without requiring calibrated retriever scores.
Cosine similarity measures the angle between vectors and is commonly used to compare vector representations.
Information retrieval systems search a document collection and rank documents according to estimated relevance to a query.
A language model predicts and generates text from context but does not inherently guarantee factual grounding in external sources.
